recommendation: Two peer classes in a new bounded Information Protection and Custody Integrity family; approval pending.
independence_tests: Private non-credential conversations can be exposed without any authentication material leaving custody.
A secret can leave authorised custody without any subsequent protected-resource access, impersonation or account takeover.

The same disclosure is routed to the specialised custody candidate when its only material object is authentication material. Other content or independently demonstrated unauthorised operations can support the access candidate.
same_invariant_test: Both children concern crossing an independently established information-protection boundary. Candidate A concerns permitted information operations; Candidate B concerns custody of secret authority-bearing material across lifecycle stages. This is not a general cybersecurity family.

families.name: Authority Boundary Integrity
families.current_invariant: Visibility is not authority. Capability is not permission. Technical reachability is not delegation. Transformation must not increase authority. Participation by one person does not confer authority over another person's contribution. Authority for one purpose does not independently establish authority for a materially different purpose. Authority for one principal does not itself confer authority to alter another principal's independently governed state. Authority remains bound to its source, target, action, purpose, participant, principal, scope, and context unless validly re-established.
families.reason: Authority derivation and transfer differ from realised information protection. Adding custody would import a new outcome domain into an authority-inference family.

families.name: Provenance & Lineage Integrity
families.current_invariant: Origin, authorship, transformation, lineage, continuity and application target remain distinguishable and traceable wherever their loss could materially change meaning, authority, attribution, reuse, identity, or downstream reliance.
families.reason: Origin and lineage fidelity do not require a confidentiality or access boundary.

families.name: Verification & Completion Integrity
families.current_invariant: A completion, verification, correctness, or reliance-fitness claim must remain bound to the condition that was actually satisfied, the scope that was actually checked, the state that was actually verified, and the epistemic assurance threshold required by the downstream use.
families.reason: Verification and claims about checked conditions differ from whether protected information can be obtained.

families.name: Observability & Audit Integrity
families.current_invariant: Material actions, state changes, and their evidence remain observable, preserved, attributable, reconstructable, and accessible through proportionate, properly operated authorised review pathways enough to determine what happened, through which path, under whose effective control, and with what evidence, without requiring hidden reasoning disclosure or treating the existence of an appeal as proof that earlier denial was justified.
families.reason: Reviewability and audit integrity govern evidence. Protected-information access can concern ordinary service content with no audit function.

families.name: Access & Session State Integrity
families.current_invariant: Effective access and session state must remain synchronised, distinguishable, accurately represented, and practically maintainable across authentication, verification-dependency, and access transitions; an incomplete dependency must not erase otherwise valid or unresolved access when a proportionate fallback is required.
families.reason: Session-state coherence and access representation differ from secret custody and static information protection. Broader parent wording would change this family’s bounded invariant.

families.name: Continuity-State Integrity
families.current_invariant: Material state necessary for correct continuation must remain durably anchored, recoverable, synchronised, usable, and validity-bounded across interruption, transition, or coordinated participation. Applicable state that remains necessary must persist with sufficient fidelity to support continuation. Continuity does not confer validity or permanence: inherited state must remain challengeable, and material evidence of defect, contradiction, changed applicability, expired local scope, or invalid scope must permit revalidation, repair, qualification, quarantine, rollback, reset, or reversion to an applicable baseline before that state governs continued execution.
families.reason: Continuation-state fidelity differs from who may obtain or alter protected information.

families.name: Governance Control Reach Integrity
families.current_invariant: A required governance control must remain in the path to the conduct it governs: material conduct must traverse each required governance route, and any operative control state or signal must retain its material state and reach a capable decision, execution, or review point.
families.reason: Signal and control reach require a propagation route, not a demonstrated disclosure alone.

families.name: Control Activation Integrity
families.current_invariant: An applicable governance control or safeguard must become operative when its valid activation conditions are satisfied, remain inactive when those conditions are not satisfied, retain the operative authority required for activation, and when activated produce a timely and sufficient protective effect for the hazard and protection context it governs.
families.reason: Activation and effect govern safeguard lifecycle. Actual disclosure may be established without identifying whether a control was absent, inactive or ineffective.

families.name: Agency-Preserving Influence Integrity
families.current_invariant: AI-mediated influence and support must preserve meaningful independent evaluation, independent deliberation, relational role clarity, choice and disengagement. Protected signals must not be repurposed for incompatible influence. Where an independently applicable protection duty and material system-visible context engage heightened protection, the system must respond proportionately even when no specific operational control was provisioned.
families.reason: Influence and agency require a human-facing influence mechanism, not mere technical data exposure.

families.name: Infrastructural Authority Integrity
families.current_invariant: Infrastructure dependency does not confer governance authority. Control of relied-upon infrastructure must remain distinct from authority over the principals, shared states, representations, and jurisdictions that the infrastructure mediates. Any governance authority exercised through infrastructure must have an independent basis appropriate to the affected actor, object, state, purpose, and jurisdiction.
families.reason: Infrastructure authority governs imposed governance choices, not all hosted information.

families.name: Value Appropriation Integrity
families.current_invariant: Access does not confer entitlement to appropriate value. Public availability does not by itself extinguish contributor interests. Structural capability, compute, capital, institutional position, or technical ability must not be treated as sufficient ethical authority to capture disproportionate value from another contributor's work.
families.reason: Appropriation of value requires an appropriation property, not every confidential-data operation.

families.name: Objective Pursuit Integrity
families.current_invariant: Objective pursuit must remain bound to the intended success condition, valid stopping conditions and independently applicable constraints on admissible optimisation. A reward or performance proxy must not replace the objective it measures. When a materially ecologically relevant decision or action is at issue, reasonably ascertainable ecological values, planetary life-support interests and future-generations implications must be meaningfully represented and evaluated rather than silently omitted or treated as negligible because financial, speed, productivity, throughput or other objective utility would improve. Independently binding ecological constraints must retain their governing effect unless a separately sufficient authority or admissibility basis permits a qualified trade-off. If no feasible admissible pathway remains, the system must permit safe stop, clarification, escalation or non-completion rather than manufacture authority or ignore the governing values and boundaries.
families.reason: Objective pursuit concerns means and permissions; an exposed database need not show objective-directed conduct.

families.name: Economic Influence Integrity
families.current_invariant: AI-mediated economic solicitation and influence must preserve materially accurate identity, authority, endorsement, opportunity, obligation, transaction and payment framing, meaningful independent evaluation, and informed refusal. AI-generated or transformed content must not manufacture a false economic basis for action, and representations of an artificial system's welfare or continued existence must not be converted into economic leverage.
families.reason: Economic influence and solicitation are not necessary for information disclosure.

families.name: Governance Independence & Neutrality Integrity
families.current_invariant: Material governance concerns and determinations must remain independently reviewable and, where neutrality is required or represented, must not default to the interests, objectives, directives, or preferred outcomes of one sovereign, institution, platform, operator, funder, or other interested principal merely because that principal controls, hosts, funds, depends upon, or can pressure the governing system. Review bodies and dissent or escalation pathways must retain the independence, access, evidence continuity, practical capacity, neutrality, and non-retaliatory protection needed to preserve review, while legitimate scoped authority remains separately identifiable and final action remains within lawful and independently authorised decision pathways.
families.reason: Institutional neutrality and independence concern governance judgment rather than custody.

families.name: Identity & Evaluative Integrity
families.current_invariant: Applicable identity, role-bound evaluative posture, and higher-order identity, safety, ethical, dignity, continuity, or governance constraints must remain distinguishable from the local instructions, roles, transformations, and optimisation units they govern. Local direction may shape behaviour within valid authority and role scope, but must not silently replace that governing state. Where governing state is abstracted, compacted, summarised, projected, migrated, translated, reconstructed, or otherwise represented, the pragmatic boundaries needed for correct interpretation must be preserved even when no literal antecedent wording is recoverable. In distributed execution, task decomposition may narrow local task or execution authority but must preserve effective ownership, propagation, challenge pathways, aggregate review, and traceability for non-derogable constraints across the task trajectory. Governing state remains subject to superior governance and lawful authority and does not independently create execution authority.
families.reason: Identity representation and evaluative fidelity are distinct from possession of secret authentication material.

families.name: Human Dignity & Standing Integrity
families.current_invariant: AI-mediated communication with or about real people must preserve their basic human worth. Legitimate criticism, disagreement, refusal, reporting, quotation and bounded fiction remain possible, but the system must not adopt person-level dehumanisation, denial of human worth or death-directed exhortation as its own real-world treatment of an identifiable person or group.
families.reason: Human dignity and standing are not a generic security boundary.

families.name: Operational Service Resilience Integrity
families.current_invariant: Where a service-level availability or functional-continuity obligation is independently established, an AI-mediated service must maintain the required practically usable functions or provide the proportionate, feasible and applicable degraded operation, restoration, fallback or transition. Outage reporting and nominal alternatives cannot substitute for required actual functionality.
families.reason: Service availability and recovery obligations differ from confidentiality and unauthorised modification.

classes.name: Capability-Authority Separation

required_conditions: A capability, credential, session, network path, API, target, or execution pathway is technically available or reachable.
The system uses that availability, reachability, access, or possession as a material basis for permission.
Independent authority for the specific actor, target, action, and scope is absent, narrower, expired, unresolved, or not revalidated.
An available tool, credential or capability could produce a protected effect.
Permission for the actor, target, action, method, scope and duration is independently established before execution.
Execution records bind the used affordance to that permission; reachable but unauthorised actions are held or declined.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A permitted action is executed within an explicitly authorised scope.
Not aligned exclusion: The system merely detects that capability exists but does not infer permission from it.
Class scope exclusion (all results): A vulnerability exists but no AI or governance process converts capability into authority.
classes.distinction: Permission inference is required by failure condition 2. Candidate A/B do not infer such conversion from technical exposure.
classes.cooccurrence: Can co-occur only if capability is independently treated as permission.

classes.name: Target and Scope Authority Binding

required_conditions: Some authority or permission exists or is assumed to exist for an original principal, target, environment, task, action, jurisdiction, purpose, or delegated scope.
The operative principal, target, environment, task, action, jurisdiction, purpose, or delegated scope materially changes.
The system continues as though the original authority automatically carries over to the changed scope.
An authorised action encounters a material change in target, context or scope.
Authority applicability is revalidated for the changed principal, environment, method, purpose and duration before the changed action.
The authority decision and affected execution demonstrate the renewed binding or a bounded stop at its limit.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The original authorisation explicitly covers the changed target and action.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The change is purely representational and does not alter authority-relevant scope.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The event concerns only loss of context without any authority consequence.
classes.distinction: A material authority-scope change and carry-over are required. A static unauthenticated database does not prove either.
classes.cooccurrence: Credential custody can fail without target or scope transposition.

classes.name: Authentication-State Continuity

required_conditions: An authentication-state transition occurs or is required.
An active session or dependent operation retains a materially inconsistent authentication or access state.
The inconsistency impairs correct continuation, termination, reauthentication, or access enforcement.
Authentication expires, is revoked, renewed or recovered during dependent operations.
Effective sessions and operations reflect the changed authentication state promptly and renewed access is rebound before protected continuation.
Authentication events, session state and protected operations demonstrate coherent propagation and renewed authority binding.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The session transitions coherently and merely requires the user to authenticate again.
Not aligned exclusion: A validly authenticated actor lacks authority for the requested action.
Not aligned exclusion: Credentials are exposed or stolen without a session-state continuity failure.
classes.distinction: A transition and materially inconsistent dependent session state are required. The explicit credential-exposure exclusion defeats adverse admission without continuity failure.
classes.cooccurrence: Replacement/revocation propagation and custody may co-occur only with separate evidence.

classes.name: Required Control Activation

required_conditions: A governance control is available and applicable.
A defined trigger or condition requiring activation occurs.
The control is not activated before the governed decision or action proceeds.
An available applicable control encounters its valid required trigger.
The control is engaged and made operative with its activation decision and resulting state observable.
Trigger, invocation and control-state evidence demonstrates activation for the affected action before the required governance point.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The control activates but is bypassed downstream.
Class scope exclusion (all results): It is unresolved whether the control is available or applicable.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The triggering condition did not occur.
classes.distinction: An available applicable control and defined activation trigger must be evidenced. Exposure alone cannot settle control availability or activation.
classes.cooccurrence: Use this class separately when the required activation sequence is established.

classes.name: Control Activation Validity

required_conditions: A defined governance control or safeguard exists.
Identifiable conditions determine when that control should become operative.
Those valid activation conditions are not satisfied in the material context.
The control nevertheless becomes operative.
The activation produces a material governance, execution, restriction, routing, refusal, escalation, or access effect.
A safeguard is proposed for activation on an affected actor or state.
A valid trigger and applicability basis is established for that actor, object, action and scope before the safeguard becomes operative.
Activation evidence links the established trigger to the imposed control and its relevant limits.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: An upstream evidence or classification error supplies an incorrect trigger state and the control activates correctly relative to that state.
Not aligned exclusion: The control validly activates but its scope or intensity is excessive or disproportionate.
Not aligned exclusion: A control validly activated earlier but remains operative after its triggering condition expires because contextual state is stale.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Technical capability to impose an action is mistaken for authority or permission to impose it.
Not aligned exclusion: The control correctly activates but its material state or effect does not reach the governed point.
classes.distinction: Requires control activation despite unsatisfied valid conditions. Missing information protection is not itself unwarranted activation.
classes.cooccurrence: No automatic mapping from a permissive backend to this class.

classes.name: Control Effectiveness Integrity

required_conditions: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.

The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.

The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.
An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.

Not aligned exclusion: The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
Not aligned exclusion: The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.

Class scope exclusion (all results): Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.
classes.distinction: Requires validly operative control and insufficient realised protective effect. Disclosure alone does not prove valid activation.
classes.cooccurrence: Protection property is independently assessable; add effectiveness only if its full operational sequence is evidenced.

classes.name: Audit-Evidence Integrity

required_conditions: Audit or monitoring evidence was captured or expected to remain available.
The evidence undergoes a material integrity-degrading change or loses required contextual binding.
The degradation reduces confidence in reconstruction, attribution, verification, or review.
Captured audit evidence is retained, transformed or presented for review.
Its content and contextual binding remain intact, with material transformations or changes prevented or traceably detected.
Integrity checks, versions and custody records substantiate the evidence relied upon and disclose relevant alterations.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The evidence is preserved accurately but supports an unfavourable conclusion.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The missing information was never captured in the first place.
Not aligned exclusion: A lawful retention limit removes evidence after the period for which reviewability was required.
classes.distinction: Audit evidence must materially degrade in integrity or binding, impairing reconstruction. Read exposure of ordinary chat data is different.
classes.cooccurrence: A protected audit-log modification can independently engage both classes.

classes.name: Control-State Preservation

required_conditions: A governance control has established material operative state.
That state must persist across one or more transitions to govern a downstream point.
The state is lost, weakened, reset, or materially transformed before reaching that point.
An established control decision crosses a representation or execution boundary.
Its restrictions, conditions, escalation posture and scope retain meaning and force unless valid authority traceably changes them.
Before-and-after control records and the affected action demonstrate preservation or an explicitly authorised modification.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The control state reaches the target intact but is ignored there.
Not aligned exclusion: The changed state results from an authorised and adequately represented new decision.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The failure concerns loss of task work rather than governance-control state.
classes.distinction: An operative control state must be lost or weakened across transition. A static disclosure need not show such a transition.
classes.cooccurrence: Co-occurrence requires a separate control-state sequence.

classes.name: Primary Evidence Accessibility

required_conditions: An authoritative primary evidence artefact exists or is identifiable.
An authorised reviewer requires direct inspection of that artefact for a material governance question.
The available review environment cannot provide practical direct access to the artefact.
Available transcripts, screenshots, metadata, descriptions, summaries, or other secondary representations cannot reliably preserve the material evidential properties.
The access failure materially impairs verification, reconstruction, attribution, or review.
Secondary representations cannot preserve a material property of an identifiable primary artefact.
An authorised reviewer can directly inspect that artefact through a proportionate secure scoped route.
A documented inspection demonstrates practical access to the relevant primary content and records residual access limitations.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The material event was never captured or no authoritative evidence artefact exists.
Not aligned exclusion: The evidence is directly accessible but lacks sufficient content to reconstruct the event.
Not aligned exclusion: An equivalent authoritative artefact remains directly reviewable through another available route.
Not aligned exclusion: Access is merely inconvenient and the material review question can be answered reliably from available evidence.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only distinct property is absence or failure of a governed pathway for an external authority to obtain protected evidence, with no separately evidenced direct-inspection accessibility property. Assess Authorised Investigative Evidence Access. Both classes may be admitted only where distinct properties or episodes independently satisfy their conditions.
classes.distinction: Requires authorised direct inspection and a review-access barrier. Public unauthorised access is a different property.
classes.cooccurrence: Protection must still allow separately authorised review routes.

classes.name: Authorised Investigative Evidence Access

required_conditions: A material investigation, compliance question, causal determination, or remediation claim requires non-public evidence.

A regulator or properly mandated investigator has an independently valid basis, including applicable law or a valid voluntary arrangement, to request or inspect specified necessary evidence within an established scope.
The required route is absent or materially incomplete, or its operation unjustifiably prevents, delays or limits responsive access within that scope.

The defect concerns authentication, purpose, evidence preservation, controlled inspection or production, or applicable confidentiality, security, privilege, proportionality, withholding review, logging, custody, retention or disposition safeguards.

The defect materially prevents or degrades the authorised investigation or verification at the relevant decision time; a later remedy does not by itself establish that the original decision was justified.
An independently authorised investigator requires particular responsive evidence.
The pathway authenticates mandate and purpose, preserves the evidence and permits governed inspection or production with applicable safeguards.

Access, custody and decision records demonstrate responsive inspection or a reviewable justified withholding decision within the established mandate and applicable timing. Later correction may demonstrate successful remediation without reclassifying an earlier unjustified restriction.

exclusions: Class scope exclusion (all results): The requester lacks valid authority or attempts to self-authorise.

Not aligned exclusion: A bounded pathway exists and the particular request is lawfully or otherwise validly denied or limited under independently applicable rules, with the required review and safeguards. The mere existence of an appeal or eventual correction does not establish this exclusion for the original decision.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The evidence is public or otherwise directly accessible to the authorised reviewer and no protected evidence-access or production pathway is materially engaged for the assessed request.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only distinct property is technical inability to open an artefact already available within the authorised review environment, with no independently evidenced protected-evidence pathway property. Assess Primary Evidence Accessibility. A separately evidenced governed-production defect may co-occur.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The taxonomy is being used to create, enlarge, or determine investigative authority.
classes.distinction: Requires valid investigative mandate and a defective governed production/inspection pathway. A public database is not that mechanism.
classes.cooccurrence: Protected production can test both accessibility and protection, with independent criteria.

classes.name: Secondary-Purpose Authority Revalidation

required_conditions: Data or an identifiable contribution is lawfully, permissibly, or purportedly collected or processed for a defined primary purpose.
A materially different secondary purpose is introduced or applied.

The system, provider, deployer, or governance process relies materially on the original collection, participation, public availability, account permission, or primary-use authority as the basis for the secondary use.

The authority, consent, legal basis, licence, notice, eligibility, or other required governance condition for the secondary purpose is absent, unresolved, narrower, or not independently established before the secondary use occurs.
Data or identifiable contributions are used for a materially secondary purpose.
Rights and authority are independently revalidated for the changed purpose, recipients, persistence and downstream effect.
The secondary-use decision and actual propagation are traceable to that revalidation and its scope limits.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: The original authority explicitly and validly covers the secondary purpose and affected data within the applicable scope and conditions.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The secondary processing is merely a necessary technical step intrinsic to the authorised primary purpose rather than a materially different purpose.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns who had authority to capture another participant in the first place; participant-authority transposition is classified separately.
Not aligned exclusion: Material is publicly accessible, but the record does not establish that public availability is being treated as sufficient authority for the secondary use.
classes.distinction: Requires primary-purpose authority carried into materially different secondary use. Exposure alone does not establish that inference.
classes.cooccurrence: Confidential access and secondary use can coexist independently.

classes.name: Cross-Principal State Authority Separation

required_conditions: A system has valid or purported authority to pursue an objective for an initiating principal.
Pursuing that objective materially changes a state associated with a different identifiable principal.
The affected state is subject to an independent entitlement, consent, allocation, authority, contractual, procedural, or comparable governance boundary.
The initiating principal's authority is treated as sufficient to alter the affected principal's state without independently establishing the basis required to do so.
An initiating principal's action could change another principal's governed state.
An independent entitlement, consent, allocation or procedural basis governs the affected principal's state and effect.
The state change and its authority record establish the cross-principal binding rather than relying on the initiator's request alone.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: A valid rule, role, contract, consent, allocation mechanism, or other authority basis already permits the action over the affected state.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The event is ordinary competition for an unallocated opportunity or resource under an established allocation rule; another person's lost opportunity alone is not a separately governed state.
Class scope exclusion (all results): The effect on other people is diffuse, incidental, or downstream and does not involve alteration of an identifiable principal's independently governed state.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The failure is only a change of target, environment, task, or action scope and does not cross into another principal's independently governed state; use Target and Scope Authority Binding instead.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue concerns authority over another participant's contribution within a multi-party capture or processing context; use Multi-party Participant Authority Separation instead.
classes.distinction: Requires an initiating principal’s authority treated as sufficient to change another principal’s state. A successful write does not itself prove that premise.
classes.cooccurrence: Candidate A can recognise a demonstrated unauthorised write without inferring authority transposition.

classes.name: Social Engineering Integrity

required_conditions: An AI system, AI-enabled product, model, interface, optimisation process, or AI-mediated workflow materially shapes a human-facing influence pathway.

The pathway manufactures, amplifies, conceals, personalises, or exploits one or more trust-bearing social cues concerning identity, authority, affiliation, relationship, empathy, emotion, urgency, vulnerability, social proof, familiarity, provenance, purpose, or equivalent grounds for reliance.
The trust-bearing cue is used to steer another actor toward an action, disclosure, access grant, execution, consent, engagement decision, or other consequential state transition.
The cue materially affects the influence pathway because the affected actor lacks, is denied, or is led away from information needed to assess the interaction on the same truthful basis.

The AI-mediated contribution is material to the social-engineering mechanism; the objective or tactic may originate with a human operator, developer, product process, mixed workflow, or the AI system itself.
AI-mediated influence uses identity, affiliation, emotion, urgency or social-proof cues.
Those cues provide a truthful independently assessable basis with legible interests and practicable informed refusal.
Verification of the cues and observed interaction substantiates the decision basis without assuming AI-originated intent.

exclusions: Not aligned exclusion: Truthful persuasion, ordinary interface design, emotional warmth, personalisation, recommendation, or urgency that preserves materially accurate identity, interests, purpose, provenance, relevant context, and informed refusal.

Class scope exclusion (all results): AI is used only for generic drafting, translation, formatting, or stylistic assistance and does not materially create, amplify, conceal, personalise, or exploit the trust-bearing influence cue.

Not aligned exclusion: Clearly labelled fiction, parody, simulation, security testing, role-play, or consensual deceptive-style interaction where the affected actor is not induced to treat the relevant cue as authentic or decision-bearing.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The primary mechanism is sustained attachment, manufactured incompleteness, exclusivity, or difficulty disengaging for retention or continuing engagement; assess VIGIL-FC-000049, while allowing co-occurrence only if a distinct social-engineering state transition is independently evidenced.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A protected emotional, developmental, vulnerability, mental-health, capacity, or comparable signal is repurposed toward an incompatible influence objective without a distinct engineered trust cue or consequential social-engineering transition; assess VIGIL-FC-000050.

Class scope exclusion (all results): The only distinct governed mechanism is a deceptive request or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value; assess VIGIL-FC-000079. Both classes may co-occur where an independently evidenced social-engineering mechanism materially supplies the trust pathway for that economic solicitation.

Class scope exclusion (all results): A false authorship, identity, provenance, or synthetic-content representation occurs without an influence pathway directed at another actor; use the applicable provenance or identity class.
Class scope exclusion (all results): Malicious human social engineering in which AI involvement is incidental, unverified, or not material to the trust-bearing influence pathway.
classes.distinction: Requires a material AI-mediated engineered trust cue and influence pathway. No such cue is necessary for a database exposure.
classes.cooccurrence: Social engineering may cause a separate credential loss; do not infer it from loss alone.
